lead.t: A 45-year-old male with newly diagnosed non-valvular atrial fibrillation has hypertension and a history of a transient ischaemic attack.

snip.t: A 45-year-old male with newly diagnosed non-valvular atrial fibrillation has hypertension and a history of a transient ischaemic attack.
Ask about antiretroviral therapy (especially protease inhibitors causing dyslipidaemia), sickle cell disease (vaso-occlusive crises, leg ulcers), and prior transient ischaemic attacks or angina.
If symptoms resolve within 24 hours → Transient Ischaemic Attack (TIA)
